notes:
Account summary: Astrolabe builds an IDE-integrated copilot aimed at enterprise engineering teams. Primary product is a low-latency, token-efficient inline completion engine (editor plugins for VSCode, JetBrains) targeted at real-time UX. Key ask: "\"instant\" feel for suggestions (no perceptible stall when user pauses) while bounding cost per suggestion via token budgets and smart truncation.

Technical requirements / constraints:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: P50 <= 80ms, P95 <= 220ms; ideal P95 <= 150ms for main branch suggestions. Customer asked for explicit jitter envelope: inter-chunk jitter <30ms to avoid flicker in editor UI.
- Throughput: support 200 concurrent active sessions per region in initial Dedicated pool, scale target 1k concurrent in 6 months.
- Streaming: prefer gRPC bidi streaming but will accept SSE for hosted. Need chunked partial tokens for progressive rendering (token deltas, not full re-renders).
- Backpressure / rate control: client will signal rapid typing; want server-side backpressure to collapse existing in-flight predictions and re-route to a smaller/cheaper model variant.
- Token budget tuning: default suggestion budget = 32 tokens; dynamic budgets based on file context and prompt complexity (language heuristics). Need ability to enforce soft vs hard token caps and metadata for consumed tokens per suggestion.
- Model/version pinning: must pin to a verified model revision for reproducibility in canary and stable channels; automatic fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant on overload with transparent routing policy.
- Observability: per-token latency, chunk jitter, aborted predictions, and token cost per suggestion; require token-level traces surfaced to Console / tracing hooks.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), audit logs for prompts/responses, KMS integration for key management, data residency (EU customers), retention policy 90 days by default.

POC plan defined in-deck (linked): 2-week integration POC covering:
- Week 1: integration of SDK streaming to VSCode plugin, measure TTFT P50/P95, capture jitter and chunk counts.
- Week 2: experiment token-budget policies (32/48/64), enable KV-prefix caching for common file headers, test fallback routing under synthetic load.

POC success criteria (customer):
- TTFT P50 <= 80ms and P95 <= 200ms under realistic dev load (50 active editors).
- Per-suggestion token cost reduction >= 20% vs baseline with token-budgeting + caching.
- No user-visible flicker (inter-chunk jitter <30ms) and backpressure correctly cancels obsolete predictions.

- VP Eng: "Need it to feel instant — even 200ms stutters kill muscle memory."
- Lead SWE: "If we can pin versions and get predictable token spend, we commit."
